description: Ω5 domain pack — the email ontology as DECLARATIONS: SCHEMA (Message/Thread/Folder/Contact), CONTRACT (the six message.* ops with their risk classes — v0.2.0 appends message.receive@1, the inbound-ingest simulator contract that enables the "when Peter messages me" rule loop; D-222), POLICY (consent defaults, keep-all retention, draft→sent state machine), TEST (pack conformance dir). A pack declares the domain; a PROVIDER plugin (provider.email.file) implements the contracts. Passive v1: no ops, no capabilities, no dependencies — a pack may carry ops in a later version. Contract evolution is APPEND-ONLY: v0.1.0's five contracts are untouched; 1.x dependencies are unaffected.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: message id within ns email; provider-assigned (e.g. msg_<hex>)

fields.name: threadId
fields.doc: owning thread id; derived from (subject, to) when not supplied by the caller

fields.name: folder
fields.doc: mailbox folder name: sent | archive | trash | ... (moved via message.move@1)

fields.name: from
fields.doc: sender address; provider config from, default me@local

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: mailbox flags object {seen: boolean, flagged: boolean, draft: boolean}; message.read@1 sets seen, message.send@1 clears draft (draft→sent transition)

schema.doc: email.Message@1 — one stored email message (persisted as a vault object in ns 'email', meta.type='message').

fields.name: subject
fields.doc: thread subject (subject of the first message)

fields.name: messageIds
fields.doc: ordered message ids in this thread

fields.name: lastAt
fields.doc: epoch ms of the most recent message in the thread

schema.doc: email.Thread@1 — a conversation rollup. Declared ontology; materialized by providers from wave Ω6 on.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: folder id (the folder name used by email.Message.folder)

schema.doc: email.Folder@1 — a mailbox folder. Declared ontology; folder rows are materialized by providers from wave Ω6 on.
email.Contact@1 — an address-book entry. Declared ontology; materialized by providers from wave Ω6 on.

contract.doc: send {to, subject, body, threadId?} — leaves the local vault world (an outbound message), so consent is required by default (email.policy@1).
list {folder?, limit?} — summaries of stored messages (latest revision each), newest first, bounded.
search {q} — full-text search over stored message bodies (vault FTS), summaries back.
read {id} — the full message; marks it seen (flags.seen) as a separate internal vault revision.
move {id, folder} — internal mailbox mutation: appends a new revision with the folder changed.

receive {from, subject, body, folder?} — ingest an inbound message into the vault (folder inbox). READ risk: ingestion is vault-internal; the simulator semantics (the real leg is an IMAP provider) are documented in the provider.

policy.description: Domain policy for pack.domain-email: consent defaults, retention, and the message state machine — declarative data a law provider may consume (vivim.law v1 evaluates its own risk table; this doc is the domain's declared intent).

consent.rationale: sending mail is an external mutation of the world outside the vault (recipients, servers); reading and moving are vault-internal.

retention.notes: v1 keeps every revision (vault Merkle chain is append-only); compaction may move superseded revisions cold but never deletes them, and refs-honoring protects referenced revisions.

transitions.doc: message.send@1 materializes the message already in state sent (flags.draft=false); v1 has no persisted draft state

policy.doc: email.policy@1 — the email domain policy as data.

test.doc: pack conformance: ontology validation (schema fields complete, contract risk classes, namespace-clean ids, acyclic draft→sent state machine).

capabilities.justification: A pack is passive declarations: no ops to route, no ports to call, no host capabilities. The implementing provider (provider.email.file) carries the capabilities; this manifest only declares the domain.
